title: Detect CNAME loops in the CNAME cache while trying to resolve

timeline.message:
Detect CNAME loops in the CNAME cache while trying to resolve

Motivation:

We need to detect CNAME loops during lookup the DnsCnameCache as otherwise we may try to follow cnames forever.

Modifications:

- Correctly detect CNAME loops in the cache
- Add unit test

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/10220
timeline.author: Norman Maurer

Just code style, so not necessary: I would pack this "uncommon case" in a separate method
LGTM just that small code change, but I'm already happy

Please correct me if I'm wrong, but I think this is not sufficient.

I had a similar issue in Gatling, regarding HTTP permanent redirect cache.
It turned out the user had misconfigured his rewrite rules and ended up with circular redirects:

A -> B -> C -> A

I recommend adding a max redirect chain depth to the while loop.
Better safe than sorry.
@slandelle I think it should be good enough as `A` would be in the `Set` and so we would break. What I am missing ?
My bad, indeed, I had missed the check on the boolean returned by add.
Then, your call: perfect solution at the cost of extra HashSet allocation vs loop limit without extra allocation?
@slandelle lets keep the set for now...we can add extra options later on. We only need the set if we have more then 2 links in the chain anyway
